posts.title: Daisenpū (Nintendo Switch)
posts.description: Vertical Checkpoints ON 4 Difficulty levels 4 Stages (loopable) Ship speed fixed - - - - - - - Developed by Toaplan / Bitwave Games Published by Clear River Games in 2025 If you're familiar with the history of Toaplan you'll know that Daisenpu isn't really a standout in the library of this pivotal shmup developer. Often overshadowed by other contemporary Toaplan titles, Daisenpū was a commercial underperformer in arcades and is generally viewed by historians as an interesting, quirky detour rather than a top-tier Toaplan classic. Developed for Taito's X System hardware, it arrived right after massive genre-defining hits like Tatsujin / Truxton (1988) and right before Fire Shark / Same! Same! Same! . posts.title: Salamander III (Nintendo Switch)
posts.description: Horizontal / Vertical Checkpoints OFF 4 Difficulty levels 6 Stages (loopable) Ship speed by icons - - - - - - - Developed by M2 / Konami Published by Limited Run Games in 2025 No one expected this. Well, I didn't. Released in 2025 for a few different systems, Gradius Origins is a compilation that brings back several titles from the Gradius series and its spin-off franchise Salamander . Seeing these old titles re-appear for newer platforms was never supposed to be novelty, given the fact that such compilations had already been published in the past. There is a specific highlight that soon attracted the eyes of old timers like myself though: the inclusion of a brand-new game called Salamander III . This sequel comes almost 30 years after Salamander 2 , and also after a good number of years since the last Gradius -related game, Otomedius Excellent . posts.title: Xevious - Fardraut Densetsu (PC Engine)
posts.description: Vertical Checkpoints ON 1 Difficulty level 4 Stages Ship speed fixed - - - - - - - Developed by Compile Published by Namco in 1990 It's no secret I've never really held the original Xevious in high regard, even though I'm well aware of its importance to the development of vertical shooting games. That's why I knew very little about its sequels until recently, when I decided to see what the PC Engine port had to offer. And lo and behold, Xevious - Fardraut Densetsu actually boasts a little bit more than the drab offerings of the original, even including a proper ending in the special mode that corresponds to the game's title. This game is also considered to be the third or fourth in the series, depending on how you see it.
